tool.name: Raw file header
tool.command: #import re ## The element identifier keeps the file's original name and extension. #set $raw_name = re.sub(r'[^\w.\-]', '_', str($raw.element_identifier)) ln -s '$raw' '$raw_name' && python '$__tool_directory__/raw_header.py' '$raw_name' --name '$raw_name' --header '$header'

param.name: raw
param.label: Raw file
param.help: A raw file of a format gwyddionpy reads (e.g. Nanonis .sxm, RHK .sm4, Bruker .spm), or any file with a text header.

has_line.line: # Header of const_dos_No14_003.sxm, read with: gwyddionpy (nanonis)

has_text.text: read with: leading text; gwyddionpy: UnsupportedFormatError

has_line.line: This is not a Nanonis SXM file.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Writes the header of a raw file as text, for the ELN tools. The header is read with [gwyddionpy](https://github.com/FAIRmat-NFDI/gwyddionPy), which reads many scanning probe microscopy formats, also binary ones such as RHK `.sm4`.
If gwyddionpy cannot read the file, or finds no metadata, the header is the file's leading text: the text before the first binary byte or data marker (`[DATA]` of Nanonis `.dat` files), at most 64 kB.
-----
**Output**
A text file. Its first line names the file and how the header was read; then one `key: value` line per header entry (gwyddionpy) or the file's own header lines (leading text).
